text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on August 19 in history.
14 - Augustus, the first Roman Emperor and adopted son of Julius Caesar, died.

1477 - Maximilian I, son of Holy Roman Emperor Frederick III, married Mary of Burgundy and acquired the Burgundian possessions in the Netherlands and France. On this day in 1493, he became Roman Emperor.
1493 - Frederick III, Holy Roman Emperor, died and was succeeded by Maximilian I.
1560 - James Crichton, Scottish scholar who propounded many scientific theories and was known as "the admirable Crichton," born.
1561 - Mary Queen of Scots arrived in Scotland to assume the throne after spending 13 years in France.
1587 - Sigismund III, son of John of Sweden, was elected King of Poland. He sought a union of Poland with Sweden but instead created hostility and war between the two.
1601 - Michael the Brave, Romanian national hero, was assassinated.
1646 - John Flamsteed, British astronomer and founder of the observatory at Greenwich, born.
1743 - Comtesse Du Barry (Marie Jeanne Becu), mistress of King Louis XV of France, was born. Arrested during the Revolution 1793, she was executed on December 7 that year.
1772 - Gustav III seized effective control of the Swedish government and restored the full power of the monarchy which had been subordinate to parliament since 1720.
1812 - In the Anglo-American war of 1812, the U.S. warship Constitution defeated the British frigate Guerriere.
1839 - Details of Louis Daguerre's first practical photographic process were released in Paris.
1871 - Orville Wright, U.S. inventor and aviator, born. With his brother Wilbur, he succeeded in developing the first machine capable of powered flight in December 1903.
1878 - Manuel Luis Quezon y Molina born. He was first president of the Philippines Commonwealth established under U.S. tutelage in 1935.
1883 - Gabrielle "Coco" Chanel, French dress designer who ruled over Parisian haute couture for almost six decades, born.
1902 - American writer and poet Ogden Nash born.
1929 - Sergei Diaghilev, Russian ballet impresario and director, died. He founded his Ballets Russes produced such masterpieces as Stravinsky's "Rite of Spring" and "Firebird".
1934 - Germans voted to give Adolf Hitler the presidency in addition to being Chancellor.
1936 - Federico Garcia Lorca, leading Spanish writer and poet, was shot dead by Fascists at the beginning of the civil war.
1940 - Italian troops forced the British to withdraw from Somaliland.
1942 - British and Canadian troops launched a disastrous attack on German-held Dieppe. Of the 6,000 troops involved, only about 2,500 returned; the rest were killed or captured.
1944 - Sir Henry Wood, English conductor and co-founder of the British Promenade Concerts ("Proms") in 1895, died.
1946 - U.S. President Bill Clinton born. Governor of Arkansas 1978-80 and from 1982 until he was elected the country's 42nd president in November, 1992.
1953 - Prime Minister Mohammad Mossadeq was overthrown in a coup in Persia. General Zahedi took over and the Shah returned from exile in Italy.
1960 - The Soviet Sputnik 5 satellite was launched into Earth orbit carrying two dogs named Belka and Strelka.
1960 - Gary Powers, the U.S. spy plane pilot shot down by the Russians over Soviet territory, was sentenced to 10 years detention.
1966 - A severe earthquake in Turkey killed over 2,000.
1973 - George Papadopoulos was sworn in as president of Greece as the monarchy came to an end. He lifted martial law, in effect since 1967, but was overthrown in a coup in November.
1974 - Roger Davis, U.S. ambassador to Cyprus, was shot dead during anti-American demonstrations in Nicosia.
1977 - Actor and comedian Groucho Marx died. Probably the most popular of the famous Marx Brothers, his films included "A Night at the Opera" and "A Day at the Races".
1978 - A fire in a theatre set by Moslem extremists in Abadan, Iran, killed over 400 people.
1979 - Soviet Cosmonauts Vladimir Lyakov and Valery Ryumin returned to Earth aboard Soyuz 34 after a record 175 days in space.
1980 - 301 people died when fire swept through a Saudi Arabian airliner as it made an emergency landing at Riyadh airport.
1987 - In Britain's worst mass killing, gunman Michael Ryan shot dead 16 people during a rampage through Hungerford.
1991 - An abortive coup by hardliners against Soviet President Gorbachev began; it collapsed two days later.
1995 - U.S. peace envoy Robert Frasure and three others were killed when their vehicle plunged off a road near Sarajevo.
